Subject: Migration compatibility: OpenAI-compat API & next tests

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion about FinCo's migration goals and the constraints your engineering team is tracking (existing GCP infra, strict P95 latency targets for synchronous endpoints, and an aggressive Q3 launch). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: replace current managed inference on hyperscaler with an option that reduces per-token costs while maintaining OpenAI-compatibility for minimal code changes.
- Key success metrics: API parity (chat/completions), <=10% prompt-diff on our eval set, P95 latency <= 220ms for short-turn dialog on dedicated capacity, and stable KV cache behavior for streaming chat.
- Constraints: FinCo runs in GCP us-central with customer-owned VPC; procurement timeline ~4 weeks after POC sign-off.

Proposed immediate next tests (we can iterate):
1) OpenAI-compat swap: point an internal staging service at Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no SDK change) -> run smoke + regression on 5000 request prompt set.
2) Prompt-diff harness: run our side-by-side diff on the 300 prompt canonical set + your top 25 production prompts to quantify quality delta (we'll produce a CSV of differences).
3) Latency/throughput: spin up a Dedicated instance in us-central and run a controlled benchmark (50 concurrent clients, typical sequence lengths) to get P50/P95/P99 and token cost per 1M.

Attachments: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf (quick-run checklist) and mvp-testplan.csv (sample test harness config).

Ask from your side: can you share a 1–page listing of the top prompt templates and an example client integration? If sharing is sensitive, a redacted version is fine. Also please confirm who on the procurement side we should loop in.

Proposed times for a 45-minute technical deep-dive next week: Wed 7/7 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 7/8 09:00–09:45 PT.

Happy to coordinate — planning to loop Dylan (solutions engineer) and Ethan (infrastructure lead) once we have confirmation so they can scope the POC.

Thanks,

Rajiv — great to confirm the deep-dive for Thu 7/8 09:00 PT. Confirming next steps and deliverables so procurement and your infra team have what they need: 

1) POC scope (2 weeks):
   - Week 0 (prep): share redacted prompts + staging keys, Redwood provides SOW and test checklist.
   - Week 1: OpenAI-compat swap smoke + regression (5000 requests), prompt-diff harness run (our canonical + your 25 prompts), and a controlled latency benchmark on a Dedicated instance in us-central.
   - Deliverables: prompt-diff CSV, benchmark report (P50/P95/P99 + cost per token estimate), and a short migration guide documenting any client changes (if any).

2) SOW & procurement links: attaching redwood-poc-sow.pdf (scope + nominal costs). We'll circulate a DocuSign SOW if that looks good to procurement. Link: https://www.docusign.com/FIN-2026-78/sow

3) Technical details: our OpenAI-compat endpoint supports messages, functions, streaming, and a function_call behavior consistent with the OpenAI API. There are a couple of known differences we typically call out in migrations: 
   - Tokenization: we provide a tokenizer parity check but small tokenization differences can exist between model backends; we'll include tokenization parity results in the prompt-diff report.
   - Streaming chunk sizes may differ slightly due to our batching/throughput optimizations; developer-visible semantics remain the same.
   - SDKs: if you prefer not to change client SDKs, you can point existing clients at the OpenAI-compat URL with no code changes in most cases. If you want to adopt our SDK for advanced features (better retry/backoff and built-in KV cache helpers) that's optional and we can schedule a follow-up to scope.

4) Timing: we'll aim to have the initial POC deliverables within 10 business days after the deep-dive. Procurement timeline noted (~4 weeks).

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow.pdf, benchmark-instructions.md

I'll send calendar invites for the deep-dive and a short pre-read (checklist + test plan). Let me know if procurement needs any additional contract language up front.

Looking forward to the call.
